s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic mucocutaneous blistering disorder with oral and skin involvement
salient_findings: Small bullae, erosions, and crusts on the lower lip and oral cavity
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions on the face, trunk, and extremities
key_facts: 39-year-old woman with no significant medical history
No swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis
Superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
Negative direct immunofluorescence for IgG, IgA, and C3
Negative indirect immunofluorescence for IgG and IgA antibodies
Negative chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassays for Dsg1, Dsg3, and BP180
Positive immunoblotting for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin
Normal chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography
Normal gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy results

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive immunoblotting for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, which is characteristic of paraneoplastic pemphigus

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Mucocutaneous lesions and positive immunoblotting, although negative direct immunofluorescence

shortlist.label: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic mucocutaneous blistering disorder with oral and skin involvement

shortlist.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions and absence of mucosal involvement, but less likely due to oral cavity erosions

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely due to absence of IgG and C3 deposits on direct immunofluorescence, but still a possibility

raw.rationale: The presence of autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, as well as the clinical presentation of mucocutaneous lesions, is consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus, which is often associated with autoantibodies to these proteins and can present with a variety of skin and mucous membrane lesions.

rejected.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
rejected.why: Negative chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassays for Dsg1 and Dsg3, which are typical autoantigens in pemphigus vulgaris.

rejected.label: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
rejected.why: The presence of skin lesions and the specific autoantibody profile do not align with mucous membrane pemphigoid, which typically involves autoantibodies to BP180 or other components of the basement membrane zone.

rejected.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and autoantibody profile do not match pemphigus foliaceus, which typically involves autoantibodies to Dsg1 and presents with superficial skin lesions without mucous membrane involvement.

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The autoantibody profile and clinical presentation do not align with bullous pemphigoid, which typically involves autoantibodies to BP180 or BP230 and presents with a different pattern of skin lesions.
